order: Add a file that pins line endings to LF. Cover shell, JavaScript, and Markdown files across the repository, and mark install.sh executable as part of the same change. The goal is to stop a checkout on any platform from silently converting install.sh to CRLF, since that conversion breaks its POSIX shebang line, but leaves the installer unable to run at all on a Unix machine after a plain checkout. Scope is exactly two changes, the new line-ending rules and the executable bit, and install.sh's own contents stay unchanged, so the diff shows zero insertions inside the script. Cover only the file extensions that matter for this installer path, because widening the rule set to every text file risks rewriting files whose endings carry meaning elsewhere. Keep the fix narrow enough that a reviewer can verify its effect from one small diff alone.
claims: A new file was added, gaining 5 lines of rules for three extensions. Shell, JavaScript, and Markdown files are covered, and install.sh's executable bit was set, while no other file content changed anywhere in the tree. This keeps a checkout on any platform from corrupting the installer's shebang line, since normalization now applies to those extensions regardless of the machine's own setting. The diff was inspected line by line, and install.sh's own diff carries no content change at all, only the mode flip.
